steps.say: Most tools start with a signal and ask what followed. | Soundings works backwards. | It marks every past rise and fall, then looks at what the readings were just before each one.
Open Soundings in Angstrom Lattice. | It shows the last checked research run, for crypto or for equities.

The chart comes first. | Price on top, with a small arrow on each close a rise followed. | Below, one row per result: a dot wherever its condition held, coloured when the move followed, grey when it didn't.
Point at any day to see its price, whether the move followed, and which rows were on. | Scroll to zoom in.
Before rises lists what came before rises more often than usual. | Each result was found in the search years, then checked on later years the search never saw.
Each card shows how often a rise followed, against that coin's usual rate. | First in the search years, then in the later years.
The verdict says what happened on the later years. | Held up. A bigger move either way. Weaker later. Or faded. | The failures stay on the page: they're evidence too.
Like one? Open it as a Signal Set, then scan your assets with it in Prism, or use it in a funnel.
And How this run was done lists the settings: what counts as a rise, the coins, the years, and the rules a result had to pass.
